newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE APPROVES ISLANDERS' SALE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE APPROVES ISLANDERS' SALE.

text.p: The National Hockey League's Executive Committee Wednesday approved the sale of the New York Islanders to John Spano, with final approval by the league's Board of Governors expected by early next week.
Spano reached agreement in November to purchase the Islanders and all of the team's cable television rights from John Pickett for $165 million.
The Board of Governors' vote should come "by the end of business on Monday," NHL spokesman Arthur Pincus said.
Spano is a 32-year-old native New Yorker and chairman of The Bison Group, an aircraft and heavy equipment firm in Dallas.

Spano, who lives in Dallas and has a home on Long Island, has pledged not move the Islanders to another city. But he has stressed the need for renovations to ageing Nassau Coliseum or construction of a new arena.

Spano will become the third owner of the Islanders, a club that has fallen on hard times since its glory days of the early 1980s when the team won four consecutive Stanley Cup championships from 1980-83.
Pickett has owned the team since 1978. Roy Boe owned the Islanders for the club's first six years.
